html:
A church in the Old City of Jerusalem built over the place held since the 4th century to be where Jesus was crucified and buried. It is the holiest site in Christianity for most churches.

The emperor Constantine the Great ordered it built around 326, after a Roman temple on the site was torn down, and it was dedicated in 335. His mother Helena visited Jerusalem at this time, and legend says she found the True Cross there.

The church has been damaged and rebuilt many times. The Fatimid caliph al-Hakim had it destroyed in 1009, a deed remembered in Europe. The Byzantines rebuilt it, and after the First Crusade took Jerusalem the crusaders gave it much of its present shape. Saladin left it standing when he retook the city in 1187.

Today several churches share it, chiefly the Greek Orthodox, Roman Catholic and Armenian, under rules fixed by the Ottoman government in the 1700s and 1800s. A wooden ladder has stood on a ledge over the entrance since the 18th century because no one can agree to move it.
sum: A church in the Old City of Jerusalem built over the place held since the 4th century to be where Jesus was crucified and buried. It is the holiest site in Christianity for most churches.
